placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_lasalle, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is NOT a measurement of this frontage either: it is the line the buildings already standing on this face were built to, adopted so that the face carries one street wall rather than two (T-0104). The plat module's lot margin still fixes the side lines this run stands clear of; what it does not fix is a street line that other records had already set, and its west wall is fixed by the east wall of recon_1835_blk_south_water_lasalle_c1_08, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.
placement.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by South Water, Clark, Lake and Lasalle; standing ON the South Water Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it

persons.name: Catherine Miller
persons.note: THE ST CYR REGISTER OF 1833-1835 NAMES THIS PERSON IN THE PARISH. Read from church_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. church_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 18 October 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1).

What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

frontage.why: T-0429, and the ground it stands on was unblocked by an owner's ruling rather than found. T-0143 and T-0188 each refused to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might move, and T-0317 inherited the refusal; T-0009 closed it on 2026-08-29 under the owner's ruling that THE DRAWN SOUTH WATER LINE DOES NOT MOVE — the corridor was re-derived from committed control and data/streets/1835.json was not touched. That refusal is what had held this reach, and it is discharged. THE FACE IS THE BLOCK'S OWN, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: tools/measure_street_frontage.py reads South Water and Lake as the two faces of this block, the committed street hierarchy in data/streets/1835.json grades both `principal`, and South Water is the river street the owner's reference plate draws — 'South Water Street in 1834', roughly ten one-storey log and frame buildings shoulder to shoulder facing the river. This run is the west half of that row on this block. THE LINE IS NOT AUTHORED AT ALL, which is the difference between this run and the first deal's: the face is already built, so the run declares `adopts_face_line` and the 1.5 m is MEASURED off the three units the first deal stands on the same face — 1.4998, 1.4996 and 1.5004 m, a 0.8 mm spread — under T-0104's clause. A street wall is one wall, and this row joins one rather than opening one. THE CORNER CLAUSE BINDS AND THE FABRIC RULE AGREES WITH IT, which is the parcel's one new reading. Lot 0 is the block's free CORNER lot, at South Water and LaSalle, and the core density standard's third clause says a corner lot BUILDS TO THE CORNER: the run is anchored WEST, 1.5 m clear of the corner margin, and chains east on shared party walls. The frontage-fabric rule (T-0022) independently says a log dwelling takes the WEST END of a principal-street row where the block was dealt one, and this block was dealt a D1. On blk_randolph_market (T-0317) the corner clause and the end rule pointed in opposite directions and the parcel had to choose; here the corner clause and the fabric rule name the SAME unit, so the log cabin takes the corner and nothing has to be traded away. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the strip's two ends and the party walls between units are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the lots this run was dealt are named here so the ledger can count them rather than shared out one per unit.
